guides.title: Work the queue and the incoming work
guides.summary: Find the work that waits for a person and follow the cases that need a decision.
steps: Open "Data issues" in the left menu. The queue starts on the tasks that need a person.
Search with "Search records". The search travels in the address of the page, so the queue can be sent to a colleague.
Open "More filters" to narrow the queue by record type or by source, then click "Apply filters". The count beside each filter covers the same tasks as the rows.
Open a task. Its summary names the record, the source, the status and the next step before the comparison.
Read the "Muse guide" panel above the task. It answers from saved words: "Saved guidance."
Open "Source records" to see what each source system sent. Each row names the one action its link state asks for, such as "Review match".
Open "Activity" to see who acted, what was recorded and when.

Open "More tools" in the left menu, then "Intake queue", to see the cases the City has in front of it. Every case names its next step. "Process selected with agent" is off for this role, because an Agent Operator wakes the agent and runs it.
Open "More tools", then "Early resolution", to see the cases that wait for a person, grouped by the finding that puts them there.
guides.result: Every decision is recorded with its evidence, and the queue, the source records and the activity show what happened next.

guides.title: Use the steward assistant
guides.summary: Let the assistant gather the evidence and propose a decision, then accept, change or ignore it.
steps: On "Data issues" the steward assistant shows whether it is awake or asleep. Click "Wake" to wake it, and "Put to sleep" to stop it; the change is recorded with your name. While it sleeps, "Prepare recommendations" is off and the note says "Press Wake to wake it." The Agent Operator can also wake it. Only the Agent Operator wakes the intake and adjudication agents.
Open "Data issues" and click "Prepare recommendations". The assistant works on up to 20 tasks per press. It never runs on a timer or on its own.

Read the pill on each row: "High" when the assistant is sure, "Review" when you should read the evidence first, "Held" when the facts disagree and only a person may settle it. A one-line reason sits under the record.
Open a task. The panel "The steward assistant" shows the pill, the reason and the evidence it rests on. On a task with no recommendation yet, click "Get recommendation".

Edit the "Reason" if you wish, then click "Accept recommendation". The decision is recorded with your name. A held recommendation is never accepted, and if the record changed since it was prepared you are asked to prepare it again.

Click "Explain with Muse" to have Muse rewrite the reason in plain words. It never changes the decision or its certainty. On the hosted demonstration live Muse is on, with a daily allowance of 100 calls. When live Muse is off, or that allowance is used up, the button is off and a note beside it says why.
Click "Clear recommendation" to set a recommendation aside and decide the task with the six questions below it.

Back on "Data issues", click "Accept all high-confidence" (the button shows how many). A page lists exactly the recommendations the batch would accept. Click the button "Accept these" with the count to confirm that list. An item that changed since the list was made is skipped and named, never accepted silently.
Read "Agreement with the assistant". It gives the share you accepted unchanged and the counts behind it, over the last 7 days.
guides.result: The assistant prepares; you decide. Every accepted recommendation is a decision of record in your name, and the agreement figure shows how often you took its advice unchanged.
